metadata.source: Manually curated from Robert Caro's 'The Power Broker', NYC DOT records, and historical archives
metadata.note: Simplified centerlines for visualization. Robert Moses built or oversaw all 9 expressways.

properties.description: Robert Moses routed the expressway through the dense, working-class neighborhood of East Tremont. Construction began in 1948; the route through East Tremont was settled in 1953, when Moses's alignment was approved over a Crotona Park alternative backed by Bronx Borough President James Lyons. The main road opened in 1963 and the last interchange work finished in 1972. About 4,000 families were displaced overall, roughly 1,500 of them in East Tremont; 159 apartment buildings were demolished in East Tremont and Morris Heights. Some accounts put total displacement as high as 60,000 people.
properties.name: Cross-Bronx Expressway

properties.description: The first section (Meeker Avenue and the Kosciuszko Bridge) opened in 1939; other sections followed in the 1950s and 1960s and the road was finished in 1964. Moses's earlier projects included the Triborough Bridge and Grand Central Parkway (1936) and Henry Hudson Parkway (1937). In Brooklyn Heights it was built as a triple-cantilever under the Promenade; farther south its trench along Hicks Street separated Red Hook from the rest of Brooklyn.
properties.name: Brooklyn-Queens Expressway

properties.description: Built in stages along Manhattan's East River shoreline from the mid-1930s, with the last upgrade finished in 1966. It separates the Lower East Side, East Harlem and other East Side neighborhoods from the waterfront.
properties.name: FDR Drive (East River Drive)

properties.description: Opened in 1941 as the elevated Gowanus Parkway over Third Avenue in Sunset Park and widened into an expressway from 1957 to 1964. The structure put Third Avenue — a busy commercial street — permanently in shadow.
properties.name: Gowanus Expressway

properties.description: Its first section was completed in April 1939 for the World's Fair, and it was finished in 1956. It runs along the Harlem River through the South Bronx (Mott Haven, Highbridge), between the neighborhoods and the river.
properties.name: Major Deegan Expressway

properties.description: Built from 1957 and finished in December 1972 through the South Bronx, running along Bruckner Boulevard between Hunts Point and Longwood and the rest of the borough.
properties.name: Bruckner Expressway

properties.description: A 1.29-mile connector between the Bruckner and Cross-Bronx expressways, built 1958–1963 along the Bronx River. A planned extension north was never built. After decades of community organizing it was downgraded and converted to a boulevard, completed December 11, 2019.
properties.name: Sheridan Expressway

properties.description: Built in stages from 1940 (as the Queens–Midtown Expressway) to 1972; its Queens sections opened from 1955. With the Van Wyck and Grand Central Parkway it forms a web of highways across Queens that carries Long Island commuters to the Midtown Tunnel.
properties.name: Long Island Expressway

properties.description: Built from 1959 and finished in 1964 to connect the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge (opened 1964) with the Goethals Bridge. It cut across the center of Staten Island and helped turn the borough into a car-dependent suburb.
properties.name: Staten Island Expressway
